subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should embedded macOS Dashboard browser auth be limited to configured shared token/password injection, or should it receive native device tokens for parity with native clients?
rationale: Both directions have open linked work, and choosing wrong could either cross a credential boundary or break existing Dashboard auto-auth setups after upgrade.

options.title: Adopt shared-token-only injection
options.body: Keep native device tokens inside native websocket clients, update all macOS Dashboard browser injection callers to use only configured shared auth, and close or revise the native-token parity sibling.

options.title: Keep native-token parity
options.body: Pause or close this PR and continue with the sibling parity PR if maintainers decide the embedded browser should inherit native/operator token auth.

options.title: Delay until macOS proof exists
options.body: Leave both PRs draft until a maintainer or contributor provides a real macOS Dashboard proof showing the user impact of each policy.

recommendation.title: Adopt shared-token-only injection
recommendation.body: Keep native device tokens inside native websocket clients, update all macOS Dashboard browser injection callers to use only configured shared auth, and close or revise the native-token parity sibling.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest code-history signal on the native Dashboard and Gateway auth hardening paths touched by this decision.
